title: Rust buildings carry textured materials from CC0 sets, never flat colour
note: Walls and floors use Material::color(..).with_base_texture/normal/metal_rough from CC0 sets, panelled so the texture is not stretched.
intent: Buildings are the largest surfaces in the frame, so flat colour on them is the first thing the taste judge names. Fetch three or four CC0 surface sets (cc0__search, cc0__fetch at 1k: plaster, concrete, tile, wood) with their colour, normal and roughness maps, and make one Material per kind in on_reset: Material::color(Color::WHITE).with_base_texture(color).with_normal_texture(normal, 1.0).with_metal_rough_texture(rough). A cube's texture spans each face once (0..1 per face), so a 12 m wall drawn as one cube stretches it: draw walls as panels of about 2 m (or the material's real tile size), or better, build the shell as a GLB kit in Local Blender with world-scale UVs. Pick the kind per wall from the reset rng so neighbours differ, and vary the tint slightly so a row does not read as one block. Every wall, floor and ceiling draw goes under a tag ("building", "floor") so the checks can see it.

check.ask: Do the walls and floor in view carry a real surface texture (plaster, concrete, tile, wood) that is not stretched or smeared, rather than flat colour?
check.note: Buildings carry textured materials at an even texel size; a flat or stretched wall is the first thing the judge names.

port: The level facet makes the wall kinds once in on_reset and owns every wall, floor and ceiling draw; dressing facets add decals, never repaint walls.

evidence.note: The three.js recipe materials.buildings-not-flat, ported to the genex facade (bodycam B4).
